summary: Game crashes when replacing a block with a wall with blockstate up:false
description: Give yourself a wall using give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1 Then, place a block with no other blocks around it, and press left and right click at the same time while looking at that block and holding the wall. Then, crash.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and enter a world.  
2. Execute the command ``/give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`` to obtain a wall item.  
3. Select the wall in your hotbar and hold it.  
4. Place a solid block (any type) so that it has no other blocks adjacent to it.  
5. While still holding the wall, look directly at the placed block.  
6. Press the left mouse button and the right mouse button at the same time.  
7. Observe that the game crashes.
Observed Behavior: When the player gives themselves a wall item using the command `give @p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`, places a solitary block with no adjacent blocks, and then simultaneously presses the left‑click (attack) and right‑click (use) mouse buttons while looking directly at that block while holding the wall item, the game crashes. This behavior has been observed in snapshot 21w39a and reproduces with any type of wall, not only brick walls, resulting in an immediate termination of the client.
Expected Behavior: When the player holds a brick_wall item with the BlockStateTag {up:"false"} and attempts to replace an isolated block by pressing both mouse buttons while looking at it, the wall should be placed (or the original block should be removed) according to the specified blockstate, and the game should continue running without any error or crash. The interaction should behave like any other block placement.
